thresholds.meaning: (relative, absolute): a change is flagged when it exceeds both

highlights.title: Same outcomes, no failures.
highlights.detail: All 35 scenarios keep their direct/relay outcome; final paths 51 direct / 42 relay / 0 failed (campaign 1: 49 / 42 / 2 failed, the two lossy-link runs whose connection was closed). Lab RTT, throughput, bind and connect times are unchanged within noise; real-world RTT/throughput moved by the two internet route clusters (~34 / ~37.5 ms), not by the code.

highlights.title: Verdict accuracy: 88 right / 23 misleading / 0 wrong runs (was 81 / 28 / 2).
highlights.detail: Fixed: symmetric NAT named via hard_nat_likely (9 runs), no 'two NATs' for the NAT-less Hetzner side (6), no packet_loss on congestion (6), wrong QAD port named as a possible cause (6), no 'through a relay' for a lost direct connection (2 wrong). New: packet_loss false positives in 21 runs (20 clean lab runs whose hole punching finished during the latency phase, 1 real-world) and relay_fallback_failed on the lossy link's slow but working relay path (2).

highlights.title: Lossy link (lab-netem-pr):
highlights.detail: connection survives 3/3 (was closed in 2/3), final path direct and QUIC counters present in every run; runs 61-69 s (was 68-81 s); packet_loss hint in 2/3 (was 0/3); but the concurrency phase yields no throughput (all requests cut off at 8 s) and 2/3 runs report relay_fallback_failed because the relayed upload's count arrives later than the 3 s the bench waits.

highlights.title: Connection survival after timeouts:
highlights.detail: 0 connections lost in 93 peer runs (was 2). The bench no longer times requests out on the lossy link (cut off at 8 s instead); the listener timed out 8 requests in one run without closing the connection.

highlights.title: Regressions:
highlights.detail: (1) packet_loss false positives from hole-punching probes and reordering counted as latency-phase loss (debug/latency-loss); (2) relay_fallback_failed on a slow relay path; (3) no concurrency throughput on slow links. No measurement regressions; rw-easy-to-open's relay-first start and lower RTT/throughput are routing.
